findings.reason: A one-dimensional interval support gives a concrete expanding trapezoid: its horizontal sections link the source-distance hypothesis directly to the Minkowski-sum conclusion. This materially clarifies the relation of the two support regions even though the proof is complete. Original standalone tiles show that no figure was present.
findings.action: Added an explicitly illustrative n=1, K=[a,b], a<b space-time diagram in final Remarks, with allowed-source label and closed time-t section; caption distinguishes containment from equality.

correction: Added a support-expansion illustration and explanatory caption only; original title, Statement, Facts, Proof and all frontmatter retained (terminal whitespace normalized before appended Remarks).

diagram_math_checks.objects: Spatial coordinate x in R, time coordinate s, illustrative compact interval K=[a,b] with a<b, speed c>0, fixed 0<t<T.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These specialize the Statement hypotheses without restricting the general claim; the figure depicts only 0<=s<=t.

diagram_math_checks.relation: At each s>=0, dist(x,[a,b])<=cs iff a-cs<=x<=b+cs.
diagram_math_checks.justification: For x<a the distance is a-x, for a<=x<=b it is zero, and for x>b it is x-b. Hence the two labelled side boundaries are exactly the interval-offset endpoints. This is the one-dimensional instance of the Statement and F3 distance/Minkowski equality.

diagram_math_checks.relation: The bottom closed section is K=[a,b]; the top closed section is K+[-ct,ct]=[a-ct,b+ct].
diagram_math_checks.justification: The supplier definition of domain of influence is S+closed B_ct(0). In R the closed ball is [-ct,ct]. Both sections are drawn with filled endpoint disks, matching closed intervals; no open-base-ball assertion is made by this figure.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Source support lies inside the labelled allowed region, and solution support at t is contained in the top section.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The first is the exact Statement source hypothesis; the second is the existing conclusion proved in step 2.1. Caption expressly permits strict containment, so the pictured region does not assert actual nonzero source or solution throughout.

diagram_math_checks.relation: All four trapezoid sides are present and join at the four section endpoints.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Actual native SVG has two diagonal paths, bottom horizontal path, and top horizontal path. There is no named-node cycle or implicit closing edge. Four vertices each have degree two in the schematic boundary. Time increases upward and spatial expansion is left/right outward; this is a coordinate schematic, not a commutative diagram.
